title: Four Arrays, Sum Zero

concept.title: Split four loops into two pairs
body: You pick one number from each of four arrays and want the sum to be 0. Four nested loops cost `n^4`. Split the work in the middle: compute all sums `a + b` of the first two arrays and store **how often each sum occurs** in a map (`n^2` entries). Then for every pair `c + d` look up how many ways the sums `a + b` can equal `-(c + d)`.
This "meet in the middle" idea turns `n^4` into `n^2`. The count can be as large as `n^4` (about 2.6 * 10^10 for n = 400), so use 64-bit integers.

statement: Four arrays `a`, `b`, `c` and `d`, each with `n` integers, are given. Count the tuples `(i, j, k, l)` of positions (one position in each array, `0 <= i, j, k, l < n`) with `a[i] + b[j] + c[k] + d[l] = 0`.
inputFormat: The next four lines have the arrays `a`, `b`, `c` and `d`.

examples.note: Two tuples work: (0, 0, 0, 1) gives 1 - 2 - 1 + 2 = 0 and (1, 1, 0, 0) gives 2 - 1 - 1 + 0 = 0.

hints: Four loops are too slow for n = 400.
Store the sums of the pairs from the first two arrays in a map with their counts.
For every pair of the other two arrays, add the count of the opposite sum.

import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

solution.complexity: Time O(n^2) on average, space O(n^2).
